AMICA · WARM DAWN

A redesign of the women's safety app. Out: deep-space violet, neon cyan, glassmorphic blur, and four glowing cards competing with the panic button. In: daylight warmth, measured contrast, and one colour held back so it can only ever mean emergency.

The structural changes matter as much as the visual ones — the three notes below say what changed and why.

HIERARCHY

Only one thing on the home screen is allowed to be loud. The four tools collapsed from a 2×2 grid of glowing cards into a single quiet row, and the SOS moved down into the thumb zone where a hand actually reaches it.

The status card is new: she can see the app is working. Trust is a visible state, not a promise.

A bottom tab bar replaces push-only navigation — and Logout is no longer one tap from the SOS button.

HOLD, DON'T TAP  ·  the single biggest UX change

The old SOS fired on one tap. This one needs a 2-second hold, then gives 5 seconds to cancel — and before it commits, it says out loud exactly what it is about to set off: who gets your location, that audio starts recording, that 119 is pre-dialled.

Accidental alerts are what make people stop trusting a safety app. Standing an alert down asks for a PIN, so nobody else can end it for her.

THE ONE SCREEN THAT MUST NOT LOOK LIKE AMICA

A fake call only deters anyone if the screen is indistinguishable from a real one. No wordmark, no Warm Dawn palette, no serif — system font, platform call chrome, nothing else.

These values go straight into lib/core/constants/app_colors.dart and lib/core/theme/app_theme.dart.

Every text pairing here was measured. Three tokens failed WCAG AA on the first pass — muted plum, gold, and night muted — and were darkened or lightened until they cleared 4.5:1. The ratios are printed on the swatches.
